title: Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN) for WebRTC
summary: Specifies two ALPN labels for WebRTC. The webrtc label identifies regular WebRTC, a DTLS session used to establish keys for SRTP or data channels over SCTP. The c-webrtc label describes the same protocol with confidential variations.

eli5.summary: Two name tags a browser can show during the secure handshake to say it wants a web video call.

questions: what are the webrtc alpn labels
what is the webrtc alpn label
what does alpn do in webrtc
subtitle: Two name tags, webrtc and c-webrtc, that tell a DTLS handshake it is carrying a WebRTC call, and whether the media must stay private.

tldr.problem: A DTLS session can carry many things, so an endpoint cannot tell a WebRTC session from other DTLS uses, nor whether the media must be kept from the web application that handles signaling.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8833 defines two Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation labels: webrtc for regular WebRTC and c-webrtc for the same protocol plus a promise to keep the media confidential.
tldr.outcome: Endpoints can positively identify WebRTC and sessions that need confidentiality, but the promise covers media only, not data channels, and it is not a digital rights management mechanism.

today: RFC 8833 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2021. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why Label WebRTC Sessions
sections.content:
Web Real-Time Communication (WebRTC) uses Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) to secure all peer-to-peer communications. RFC 7301 defines Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN), a way for the two sides of a TLS or DTLS handshake to agree on which application protocol will run inside.

Using ALPN to identify WebRTC lets an endpoint positively recognise WebRTC and tell it apart from other DTLS uses. Different WebRTC uses can also be advertised, and behaviour can be limited to what suits each one. In particular, this allows sessions that need confidentiality from the application managing the signaling to be identified.
sections.eli5: When two people meet, it helps to say what they are there for. ALPN lets two computers say 'we are doing a web video call' before they start.

sections.title: The Two ALPN Labels
sections.content:
The RFC defines two identifiers. webrtc means the DTLS session is used to establish keys for the Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (SRTP), known as DTLS-SRTP (RFC 5764), and the DTLS record layer is used for WebRTC data channels (RFC 8831). c-webrtc means confidential WebRTC, where peers agree to maintain the confidentiality of the media.

Both describe the same basic protocol. SRTP or data channels may be absent. Data channels send the Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) over the DTLS record layer, which can be multiplexed with SRTP on the same UDP flow. WebRTC requires Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) to set up that UDP flow, but the identifier does not cover it.

There is no functional difference between the labels, except that an endpoint negotiating c-webrtc promises to preserve the confidentiality of the media it receives.

Client role
A client that does not know whether it needs confidentiality MUST offer both identifiers.
Server role
A server that prefers neither SHOULD select webrtc.

An endpoint that requires confidentiality MUST abort the session if it does not successfully negotiate c-webrtc. A peer willing to accept webrtc SHOULD assume that a peer that does not support this specification negotiated webrtc, unless signaling says otherwise. A peer MUST NOT assume c-webrtc was negotiated unless it was explicitly negotiated.
sections.eli5: There are two name tags that otherwise mean the same thing. Wearing the second one means 'I promise to keep this private'. If you need that promise and do not get it, you leave.

sections.title: What Media Confidentiality Means
sections.content:
Private communications in WebRTC depend on separating control (signaling) from access to media. An application can then manage the signaling for a session without having access to the media. Without a signal securely bound to the session, an endpoint cannot tell whether a session requires this protection. The ALPN identifier provides that signal.

A browser is required to enforce the protection using isolation controls similar to those used for cross-origin protections in web content. The application cannot read or modify the contents of a protected media flow. Media from a c-webrtc session MUST only be displayed to users.

The promise does not apply to data sent on data channels. No mechanism currently exists to take advantage of data confidentiality, and the RFC says alternative labels might be provided in the future, for example for confidential peer-to-peer file transfer.

No specific authentication method is defined: an endpoint that accepts a session with this identifier MUST respect confidentiality whatever identity is attributed to the peer. RTP middleboxes and entities that forward or record content for others MUST NOT offer or accept a session with c-webrtc.
sections.eli5: It is like a phone call where the switchboard operator sets up the call but is not allowed to listen in. The browser makes sure the website cannot peek at the video or sound.

sections.title: The Limits of the Promise
sections.content:
Confidential communications depend on more than an agreement from browsers. Peer authentication is necessary so that data goes only to the intended peer, and information is not confidential if it is displayed to people other than those it was meant for.

The RFC states that this is not a digital rights management mechanism. A user can still record or forward media with screen recorders, tape recorders or portable cameras, and nothing technical protects media that others nearby can see or hear. The only guarantee is that the media was delivered to the user who was authenticated; users still have to judge how their peer will treat what they receive.

On a shared platform like a browser, other web applications might compromise confidentiality. For example, an application with microphone access might sample confidential audio playing through speakers, even with acoustic echo cancellation, and a camera might capture reflections. Implementations MAY limit concurrent access to input devices during confidential sessions.
sections.eli5: The promise only means the video went to the right person. It cannot stop that person from filming their screen with a phone, or someone in the room from overhearing.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: Two entries were added to the ALPN Protocol IDs registry established by RFC 7301. The webrtc label has the protocol name 'WebRTC Media and Data' and the identification sequence 0x77 0x65 0x62 0x72 0x74 0x63. The c-webrtc label has the protocol name 'Confidential WebRTC Media and Data' and the identification sequence 0x63 0x2d 0x77 0x65 0x62 0x72 0x74 0x63. Both point to RFC 8833 as the specification.
sections.eli5: The two name tags were written in the official list of allowed names, so nobody else can use them for something different.

cells: Keep received media confidential; not extended to data channels
